facts: The phone match key: the digits of the number only (`+1 (555) 123-4567` -> `15551234567`, the E.164 number without its `+`), unsalted SHA-256. A value with fewer than 7 or more than 15 digits (E.164's limit) is not a phone number and gets no key. Server use only; the raw number is never logged.

ai.title: Add phone hash function for CAPI match keys
ai.summary: Adds `hashMatchingPhone` to `common/src/matching-hash.ts` to support phone number matching in the Conversions API. The function extracts digits from a phone string, discards values with fewer than 7 or more than 15 digits, and returns an unsalted SHA-256 hex digest. This mirrors the existing `hashMatchingEmail` utility and is intended for server-side use only.
ai.evidence: The diff in `common/src/matching-hash.ts` adds the export `hashMatchingPhone` and its implementation, which extracts digits via regex, validates a length between 7 and 15, and returns an unsalted SHA-256 hex digest.

facts: The CLI's inline LINK ad: one line at the end of an answer — the ad's copy, underlined, then a dim "Ad" — drawn in place of the end-of-answer card.

Two switches must both say yes before the CLI draws it: - the server policy's `inlineAdStyle` is `link` (`INLINE_LINK_AD_LIVE` in `packages/internal/src/ad-serving/ad-policy.ts`, live for Web/Desktop); - this file's {@link CLI_INLINE_LINK_AD_LIVE}.

The CLI gate is separate because a change of CLI ad format needs the ad network's written approval (#10807), which Web/Desktop's switch says nothing about. With the gate off the CLI requests and draws exactly the card it drew before this file existed.

Whether the CLI may draw the inline link ad when the policy asks for it. A checked-in constant, not an env var: flipping it is a reviewed one-line PR and a CLI release, after the ad network's written approval.

the CLI draws an answer's inline ad: `link` only when the CLI gate is on AND the policy said `link`. An unresolved policy, a failed one, an older server without the field and any other value all draw the card.

ai.title: Add inline link ad gate and CLI link placement
ai.summary: A new module cli/src/ads/inline-link-ad.ts provides the logic and constants to render a one-line link ad in place of the end-of-answer card in the CLI, gated behind the checked-in CLI_INLINE_LINK_AD_LIVE constant and the server policy's inlineAdStyle. The CLI's ad hook and blocks renderer were updated to request and draw the link variant when both conditions are met, while the shared placement registry in the common package registered the new 'Inline-Link-After-Agent-CLI' slot and its iOS/Android equivalents. This mechanism mirrors the existing Desktop link ad, but the CLI's gate remains off by default so the current card layout is preserved until the ad network approves the format.
ai.evidence: The new file cli/src/ads/inline-link-ad.ts defines the constants CLI_INLINE_LINK_AD_LIVE (set to false), CLI_INLINE_LINK_PLACEMENT_ID, and the function inlineAdRequestPlan; common/src/constants/freebuff-placements.ts adds the 'Inline-Link-After-Agent-CLI' slot to ORIGINAL_PLACEMENT_SLOTS and its native counterparts to ios-placements.ts and android-placements.ts.
ai.unknowns: The ad network's written approval process and the timeline for enabling the CLI gate are not shown in the diff.

changes.what: Adds inline link ad gate, rendering logic, and integration with the ad request hook and block renderer.

eli5.text: The terminal version of the free AI coding assistant now has the groundwork to display ads as a single underlined link at the end of an answer, instead of the current boxed card. This new format is currently turned off for terminal users; it is only active on the web and desktop versions, and terminal use will remain unchanged until the ad network approves this specific link style and the software team enables it. No action is needed, and the way the assistant looks and works in your terminal has not changed.
